sources.entry: DatWeatherDoe - Simple menu bar weather app for macOS written in Swift.

summary.one_liner: DatWeatherDoe is a simple macOS menu bar weather app written in Swift that fetches current weather by location services or latitude/longitude.
summary.what_it_does: The app runs in the macOS menu bar and shows weather for either the device's location (via Location Services) or manually entered latitude and longitude. It refreshes on a configurable polling interval and supports dark mode. The README says it requires macOS 13.0 or later. It previously used OpenWeatherMap API 2.5, which the README says is ending in June 2024; the app now uses WeatherAPI. Developers build it themselves by adding their own WeatherAPI key to a Config.xcconfig file. The README also includes a Homebrew Cask install option.
use_cases: check current weather from the macOS menu bar
see local weather without opening a browser
show weather for a specific latitude and longitude
install a lightweight weather widget on a Mac
build and run a Swift weather app with a WeatherAPI key
how_to_run: Get a personal API key from WeatherAPI
Build and run the project in Xcode
Grant Location Services permission in System Preferences > Security & Privacy > Privacy > Location Services if using location
notable: Menu bar app with no dock presence implied by its menu bar placement
Fetches weather by Location Services or manual latitude/longitude
caveats: Developers must supply their own WeatherAPI key in Config.xcconfig
Earlier OpenWeatherMap API 2.5 support ended in June 2024; the app now depends on WeatherAPI
